resources.string: Shared-phone profiles for a device that hides them
This app cannot create real Android users - nothing can, without root. What it can do is give each person who uses this phone a separate, PIN-locked, encrypted space inside one install.

What is and is not possible here

• Real Android users/profiles are created by the system server, which demands CREATE_USERS (signature|system). A sideloaded APK can never hold it.
• OEMs disable the feature by setting config_multiuserMaximumUsers to 1; the Settings menu entry is only the visible symptom. There is no API for an app to change that value.
• So: this app isolates data, not processes. Two profiles here share one Linux UID, one notification shade and one app list. Do not treat it as a security boundary against a determined attacker holding an unlocked phone; treat it as separation between family members who share a device.
• The one system-enforced option that needs no root is a managed (work) profile, offered under “Work profile route”. It is a second user in every way that matters, but it is designed for a device policy controller, not for a second person.
A work profile is the closest real thing to a second user

Android Enterprise lets a “device policy controller” ask the system to create a managed profile: separate apps, separate encryption key, separate settings, badged icons, and its own copy of every app. No root needed. Two hard conditions apply, and neither is in this app’s control: the firmware must still support android.software.managed_users, and becoming the profile owner in this way is a one-way door that only opens when the app is the only app-owner candidate on the device.
